events.title: AlexNet wins ImageNet (ILSVRC 2012)
events.summary: A GPU-trained deep convolutional network from Hinton's Toronto lab won ILSVRC 2012 with 15.3% top-5 error versus 26.2% for the runner-up.
events.significance: Interpretation: Converted the field to deep learning on GPUs almost overnight and tied AI progress to commodity NVIDIA hardware plus large labeled datasets.

events.title: word2vec dense word embeddings
events.summary: Mikolov et al. at Google released word2vec, efficiently learning vector word representations from large unlabeled corpora.
events.significance: Interpretation: Made 'learn representations from raw text' the default in NLP, a precursor of self-supervised pretraining.

events.title: DeepMind DQN learns Atari from pixels
events.summary: DeepMind's Deep Q-Network learned many Atari games from raw pixels using one architecture.
events.significance: Interpretation: Made deep reinforcement learning the leading candidate path to general agents for the rest of the decade.

events.title: Google acquires DeepMind
events.summary: Google agreed to acquire London-based DeepMind; the price was not disclosed and press reports ranged roughly $400-650M. It followed Google's 2013 purchase of Hinton's DNNresearch and Facebook's creation of FAIR under LeCun (Dec 2013).
events.significance: Interpretation: First large bet on an explicitly AGI-oriented lab; set the pattern of hyperscalers owning or funding frontier labs.

events.title: Generative adversarial networks
events.summary: Goodfellow et al. introduced GANs, training a generator against a discriminator.
events.significance: Interpretation: Opened modern generative modeling of images; the generative lineage later passed to diffusion models in 2021-22.

events.title: Bostrom's 'Superintelligence' frames AI existential risk
events.summary: Nick Bostrom published Superintelligence, arguing advanced AI could pose an existential risk.
events.significance: Interpretation: Gave a then-fringe risk concern an academic vocabulary that influenced OpenAI's founders and, later, the 2023 statements on extinction risk.

events.title: Sequence-to-sequence learning and attention
events.summary: Sutskever, Vinyals and Le published LSTM encoder-decoder translation; Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio introduced attention the same month.
events.significance: Interpretation: Established end-to-end neural language generation; attention became the core of the Transformer three years later.

events.title: Google open-sources TensorFlow
events.summary: Google released TensorFlow as open source on 9 November 2015.
events.significance: Interpretation: Treated frameworks as strategic distribution for cloud and talent; frameworks then commoditized (PyTorch overtook TensorFlow in research).

events.title: ResNet surpasses estimated human ImageNet error
events.summary: Microsoft Research's 152-layer residual networks won ILSVRC 2015 with 3.57% top-5 error.
events.significance: Interpretation: Residual connections made very deep networks trainable and became a component of the Transformer; vision benchmarks began to saturate.

events.title: OpenAI founded as non-profit with $1B pledged
events.summary: OpenAI launched as a non-profit research company with $1 billion in total commitments from Altman, Musk, Brockman, Thiel, Hoffman, AWS, Infosys and others.
events.significance: Interpretation: Created a lab explicitly aimed at AGI outside big tech; its later scaling bet and capital structure reshaped the industry.

events.title: AlphaGo defeats Lee Sedol 4-1
events.summary: DeepMind's AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol 4-1 in Seoul in March 2016, years before many experts expected Go to fall.
events.significance: Interpretation: A public 'Sputnik moment', especially in China and Korea, that raised AI to a national-strategy priority.

events.title: NVIDIA Pascal P100 and DGX-1; first DGX-1 to OpenAI
events.summary: NVIDIA launched the P100 and DGX-1 system for deep learning; Jensen Huang delivered the first DGX-1 to OpenAI in August 2016.
events.significance: Interpretation: NVIDIA repositioned from gaming to deep-learning systems; its FY2017 filing attributed 145% datacenter growth to deep learning training.

events.title: Google discloses the TPU
events.summary: Google revealed it had used custom Tensor Processing Units for inference in its data centers for over a year.
events.significance: Interpretation: First evidence that hyperscalers would design their own AI silicon; the TPU line later trained PaLM and Gemini.

events.title: DeepMind ML cuts Google data-center cooling energy by up to 40%
events.summary: DeepMind reported its system reduced energy used for cooling in Google data centers by up to 40%.
events.significance: Interpretation: Energy entered the AI story as an application area, not yet as a binding constraint on AI itself.

events.title: NVIDIA Volta V100 with Tensor Cores
events.summary: NVIDIA introduced the Volta V100 with Tensor Cores; it began shipping in the first half of NVIDIA fiscal 2018 and drove datacenter revenue to $1.93B, up 133%.
events.significance: Interpretation: Dedicated matrix-math units made GPUs AI-specific accelerators, widening NVIDIA's lead over CPUs.

events.title: Google declares an 'AI-first' strategy at I/O
events.summary: Sundar Pichai described Google's shift from mobile-first to AI-first and announced Cloud TPUs.
events.significance: Interpretation: Defined the period's belief that incumbents with users and data would capture AI value by embedding it in existing products.

events.title: 'Attention Is All You Need': the Transformer
events.summary: Google researchers introduced the Transformer, built entirely on attention.
events.significance: Interpretation: Its parallelizable architecture made scaling on GPUs/TPUs efficient and became the substrate of every later foundation model.

events.title: China's New Generation AI Development Plan
events.summary: China's State Council set a goal of world leadership in AI by 2030 with a core industry over 1 trillion yuan.
events.significance: Interpretation: Turned AI into an explicit US-China strategic competition, foreshadowing chip export controls.

events.title: AlphaGo Zero and AlphaZero: superhuman play from self-play
events.summary: AlphaGo Zero (Oct 2017) learned Go without human data; AlphaZero (Dec 2017) generalized to chess and shogi. AlphaGo Zero remained the largest training run by compute until August 2021 (Epoch).
events.significance: Interpretation: Reinforced the belief that RL plus search, not language modeling, was the frontier path; RL returned in 2024-25 inside LLM reasoning.

events.title: OpenAI 'AI and Compute': 3.4-month doubling
events.summary: OpenAI estimated compute in the largest training runs had grown more than 300,000x since 2012, doubling every 3.4 months.
events.significance: Interpretation: Reframed AI progress as a compute-supply story, the intellectual basis for OpenAI's capital-raising strategy.

events.title: Pretrain-then-fine-tune: ELMo, GPT-1, BERT
events.summary: ELMo (Feb 2018), OpenAI's GPT-1 (Jun 2018) and Google's BERT (Oct 2018) showed self-supervised pretraining on unlabeled text transfers to many tasks.
events.significance: Interpretation: Made language-model pretraining the NLP default; BERT was the consensus winner, while GPT's generative decoder approach was the minority that later dominated.

events.title: GPT-2 and staged release
events.summary: OpenAI announced the 1.5B-parameter GPT-2 and initially withheld the full weights over misuse concerns, releasing it in stages through November 2019.
events.significance: Interpretation: First time a lab treated a language model's capability as a release-policy question; previewed later open vs closed debates.

events.title: OpenAI LP 'capped-profit' structure
events.summary: OpenAI created a capped-profit company governed by its non-profit, capping first-round returns at 100x.
events.significance: Interpretation: Acknowledged that frontier AI needs billions in capital; the hybrid governance later produced the November 2023 board crisis.

events.title: NVIDIA agrees to buy Mellanox for $6.9B
events.summary: NVIDIA agreed to acquire interconnect maker Mellanox; it closed in April 2020 and contributed 10% of NVIDIA revenue in FY2021.
events.significance: Interpretation: Extended NVIDIA from chips to data-center systems; networking became part of its moat in the cluster era.

events.title: Sutton's 'The Bitter Lesson'
events.summary: Richard Sutton argued that general methods leveraging computation ultimately beat human-knowledge-based approaches.
events.significance: Interpretation: Became the canonical statement of the scaling worldview, still a minority position in academia at the time.

events.title: US adds Huawei to the Entity List
events.summary: The US Commerce Department restricted Huawei's access to US-origin technology.
events.significance: Interpretation: Started using semiconductor supply chains as a geopolitical weapon, the template for the 2022 AI chip controls.

events.title: Strubell et al. quantify energy cost of NLP training
events.summary: An ACL 2019 paper estimated the energy and carbon costs of training large NLP models.
events.significance: Interpretation: First widely cited warning that AI's energy footprint mattered, though at 2019 scale it was framed as an environmental concern, not a capacity constraint.

events.title: Microsoft invests $1B in OpenAI
events.summary: Microsoft invested $1B in OpenAI, with Azure as exclusive cloud provider.
events.significance: Interpretation: Created the hyperscaler-lab coupling (compute for equity and exclusivity) that defined frontier AI economics afterwards.

events.title: Kaplan et al. 'Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models'
events.summary: OpenAI showed language-model loss falls as a smooth power law in parameters, data and compute over more than seven orders of magnitude.
events.significance: Interpretation: Made capability gains predictable enough to justify large capital commitments; its parameter-heavy recipe was revised by Chinchilla in 2022.

events.title: Microsoft's Azure supercomputer for OpenAI
events.summary: Microsoft said it built for OpenAI one of the world's top five supercomputers with 285,000+ CPU cores and 10,000 GPUs. The same month NVIDIA launched the A100.
events.significance: Interpretation: Bespoke hyperscaler clusters for one lab became the unit of frontier competition.

events.title: GPT-3 and the OpenAI API
events.summary: OpenAI published GPT-3 (175B parameters, ~3.14e23 FLOP) showing few-shot in-context learning, and opened a commercial API in June 2020. Microsoft took an exclusive license to GPT-3 in September 2020.
events.significance: Interpretation: Demonstrated that one general model could be prompted for many tasks, and introduced model-as-API as a business.

events.title: AlphaFold 2 at CASP14
events.summary: DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 reached a median GDT of ~92.4 at CASP14, competitive with experimental structure determination for many proteins.
events.significance: Interpretation: Strongest evidence yet of AI producing scientific value; recognized with the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (hindsight).

events.title: Global semiconductor shortage
events.summary: Pandemic demand shifts and supply disruptions produced a chip shortage that cut auto production through 2021.
events.significance: Interpretation: Made semiconductor supply chains a political issue, feeding the CHIPS Act; AI-specific supply limits (CoWoS, HBM) arrived later.

events.title: European Commission proposes the AI Act
events.summary: The Commission proposed a risk-based regulation for AI systems.
events.significance: Interpretation: Its pre-LLM, use-case-based design had to be retrofitted for general-purpose models in 2023.

events.title: Anthropic founded ($124M Series A)
events.summary: Former OpenAI researchers including Dario and Daniela Amodei announced Anthropic with a $124M Series A.
events.significance: Interpretation: Institutionalized 'safety-focused scaling' and created a third frontier lab later backed by Amazon and Google.

events.title: GitHub Copilot technical preview
events.summary: GitHub launched a Copilot preview powered by OpenAI Codex; general availability followed June 2022 at $10/month.
events.significance: Interpretation: First mass-market paid LLM product, showing coding as the first high-value use case and incumbents' distribution advantage.

events.title: 'On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models'
events.summary: Stanford CRFM coined 'foundation models' for broadly trained models adaptable to many tasks.
events.significance: Interpretation: Gave academia and policymakers a shared frame; the term later entered the EU AI Act and US EO.

events.title: Chain-of-thought prompting
events.summary: Wei et al. showed prompting large models with intermediate reasoning steps sharply improved reasoning performance.
events.significance: Interpretation: First evidence that spending more inference tokens on reasoning raises capability, the seed of 2024-25 reasoning models.

events.title: NVIDIA announces H100 (Hopper)
events.summary: NVIDIA announced the H100 with a Transformer Engine supporting FP8.
events.significance: Interpretation: The chip of the generative-AI boom; demand for it in 2023 far exceeded supply.

events.title: InstructGPT: RLHF makes small models preferred over GPT-3
events.summary: OpenAI showed outputs of a 1.3B RLHF-tuned model were preferred over 175B GPT-3.
events.significance: Interpretation: Post-training, not only pretraining scale, became a key lever for usefulness.

events.title: Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling
events.summary: DeepMind's 70B Chinchilla, trained on 1.4T tokens with Gopher's compute, outperformed Gopher (280B) and GPT-3.
events.significance: Interpretation: Shifted the bottleneck from parameters to training data and made smaller, cheaper-to-serve models the target.

events.title: PaLM 540B on Pathways/TPU v4
events.summary: Google trained the 540B dense PaLM on 6,144 TPU v4 chips (~2.56e24 FLOP).
events.significance: Interpretation: Showed Google's vertically integrated TPU stack was competitive at the frontier.

events.title: Diffusion image generation goes public: DALL-E 2, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion
events.summary: DALL-E 2 (April), Midjourney's open beta (July) and the openly licensed Stable Diffusion weights (22 Aug 2022) brought text-to-image generation to the public. They built on CLIP/DALL-E (Jan 2021) and open datasets such as LAION-5B.
events.significance: Interpretation: First consumer generative-AI wave and first proof open weights could spread a capability overnight; 'generative AI' became an investment category before ChatGPT.

events.title: CHIPS and Science Act
events.summary: The US enacted roughly $52.7B in semiconductor support including ~$39B in manufacturing incentives.
events.significance: Interpretation: Industrial policy aimed at physical supply-chain resilience, a precursor to treating AI infrastructure as national infrastructure.

events.title: US export controls on advanced AI chips to China
events.summary: BIS restricted exports to China of A100/H100-class AI chips and advanced chipmaking equipment.
events.significance: Interpretation: Made compute access an instrument of state power and split the AI hardware market geographically.

events.title: ChatGPT launches
events.summary: OpenAI released ChatGPT, fine-tuned from GPT-3.5 with RLHF, as a free research preview on 30 Nov 2022; UBS estimated 100M monthly users by January 2023.
events.significance: Interpretation: Turned LLMs from a developer API into a mass consumer product and triggered the capital and policy response of 2023.

events.title: Microsoft's multibillion investment in OpenAI
events.summary: Microsoft announced a multiyear, multibillion-dollar investment in OpenAI, widely reported as $10B.
events.significance: Interpretation: Set the template of hyperscaler capital in exchange for compute consumption and model rights.

events.title: Microsoft launches GPT-powered Bing
events.summary: Microsoft launched Bing chat on a next-generation OpenAI model (later confirmed as GPT-4).
events.significance: Interpretation: Opened the incumbent-distribution battle over search; Google's search share proved more resilient than expected (hindsight).

events.title: Meta LLaMA released and weights leak
events.summary: Meta released LLaMA (7B-65B) under a research license; LLaMA-13B outperformed GPT-3 on most benchmarks; weights leaked publicly in early March.
events.significance: Interpretation: Launched the open-weight ecosystem; capability at a given size became reproducible and commoditizing.

events.title: GPT-4
events.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-4 on 14 March 2023, with near-human results on many professional exams and no disclosure of size, compute or data; Epoch estimates ~2e25 FLOP.
events.significance: Interpretation: Set the frontier benchmark that competitors took most of 2023 to approach; ended routine disclosure of training details.

events.title: CAIS one-sentence statement on extinction risk
events.summary: Hundreds of researchers and lab leaders signed a statement that mitigating AI extinction risk should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war. It followed the FLI 'pause' letter (22 Mar 2023) and Geoffrey Hinton's departure from Google to speak about AI risk (1 May 2023).
events.significance: Interpretation: Lab CEOs publicly endorsing extinction-risk framing helped set up the Bletchley summit and the EO.

events.title: Llama 2 open weights for commercial use
events.summary: Meta released Llama 2 (7B-70B) with chat variants, free for most commercial use, with Microsoft as preferred partner.
events.significance: Interpretation: Legitimized open weights as a corporate strategy (commoditize the complement).

events.title: NVIDIA data-center revenue doubles in a quarter amid H100 shortage
events.summary: NVIDIA reported $10.32B quarterly data-center revenue, more than double the prior quarter, with H100 supply constrained; FY2024 data-center revenue reached $47.5B, up 217%. NVIDIA had briefly passed a $1T market value on 30 May 2023.
events.significance: Interpretation: The ChatGPT demand shock showed up first and most clearly in GPU revenue.

events.title: Amazon to invest up to $4B in Anthropic
events.summary: Amazon agreed to invest up to $4B in Anthropic, with AWS as primary cloud and use of Trainium/Inferentia chips.
events.significance: Interpretation: Every hyperscaler now had a frontier-lab partner; custom silicon was part of the deal.

events.title: US Executive Order 14110 on AI
events.summary: The order required developers of models trained above 1e26 operations to report training and red-teaming to the government.
events.significance: Interpretation: First US rule keyed to training compute, treating FLOP as a regulatory proxy for risk; revoked in January 2025 (hindsight).

events.title: Bletchley Park AI Safety Summit
events.summary: 28 countries plus the EU, including the US and China, signed the Bletchley Declaration on frontier AI risks on 1-2 Nov 2023.
events.significance: Interpretation: First intergovernmental agreement on frontier AI risk; spawned national AI safety institutes.

events.title: OpenAI DevDay: GPT-4 Turbo price cut, GPTs, Assistants API
events.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-4 Turbo at $10/$30 per 1M input/output tokens (a third and a half of GPT-4's launch prices) plus custom GPTs and an Assistants API.
events.significance: Interpretation: Price per capability began falling fast; OpenAI tried to become a platform rather than only a model vendor.

events.title: OpenAI board fires and reinstates Sam Altman
events.summary: OpenAI's non-profit board removed Altman on 17 Nov 2023; after a staff revolt and Microsoft's offer to hire them, he returned with a new board on 21-22 Nov.
events.significance: Interpretation: Showed that capital, compute partners and talent outweighed non-profit governance at frontier labs.

events.title: Google launches Gemini 1.0
events.summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 1.0 (Ultra, Pro, Nano), natively multimodal and trained on TPUs.
events.significance: Interpretation: Google's first credible GPT-4-class response; signalled the frontier would be a multi-player race.

events.title: EU AI Act political agreement
events.summary: EU co-legislators reached a provisional agreement on the AI Act, adding obligations for general-purpose AI models.
events.significance: Interpretation: First comprehensive binding AI law, retrofitted for foundation models.

events.title: Mistral's Mixtral 8x7B open sparse MoE
events.summary: Mistral released Mixtral 8x7B under Apache 2.0, a sparse mixture-of-experts using ~13B of ~47B parameters per token, matching or beating GPT-3.5 on many benchmarks.
events.significance: Interpretation: Brought MoE into the open-weight mainstream and showed GPT-3.5-class quality had become cheap and widely available.

events.title: New York Times sues OpenAI and Microsoft
events.summary: The NYT filed a copyright suit alleging unlicensed use of its articles for model training.
events.significance: Interpretation: Turned training-data provenance into a legal and commercial bottleneck, pushing labs toward data licensing.

periods.label: Deep learning becomes practical
periods.boundaryRationale: Starts with the 2012 demonstrations that scale works: Google's unsupervised 'cat' network (June 2012) and AlexNet's ILSVRC win (results autumn 2012, 15.3% vs 26.2% top-5 error). Ends before the Transformer (June 2017). Proposed revision: the substantive boundary is 2017-06 (Transformer) rather than 2016-12; Jan-May 2017 (PyTorch release, V100 announcement, Google's 'AI-first' I/O) still belongs to the vision/RL-centric, supervised-learning worldview. Keeping 2016-12 is acceptable for charting by calendar year.
periods.consensus: Deep neural networks trained on GPUs with large labeled datasets had overtaken hand-engineered features in vision and speech, and ImageNet-style supervised learning was the paradigm. Big tech treated deep learning as a capability to embed in existing products (search, ads, photos, speech, translation) and competed mainly for scarce researchers through acqui-hires. Deep reinforcement learning on games (DQN, AlphaGo) was widely seen as the path toward more general agents; talk of AGI was confined to DeepMind, the newly founded OpenAI and a small community.

minorityViews.view: Scaling hypothesis: simply training much larger networks on much more data would keep producing qualitatively better results; AGI timelines driven by compute growth.
minorityViews.heldBy: Ilya Sutskever (NeurIPS 2014 seq2seq talk framing), Shane Legg (~2028 AGI forecasts), DeepMind/OpenAI founders
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: became the operating thesis of OpenAI (2018-2020) and the basis for scaling-law-driven investment; largest-run compute grew ~300,000x 2012-2018.

minorityViews.view: Unsupervised/predictive (self-supervised) learning, not labeled supervision or RL, is where most learning should come from ('the cake').
minorityViews.heldBy: Yann LeCun (NeurIPS 2016), Mikolov et al. via word2vec
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: self-supervised next-token pretraining became the core of all foundation models; RL ended up as the 'cherry' in RLHF and later reasoning training.

minorityViews.view: Advanced AI poses existential risk and control must be solved in advance.
minorityViews.heldBy: Nick Bostrom, Eliezer Yudkowsky, Stuart Russell, Elon Musk; Amodei et al. framed practical ML safety problems (2016)
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: mainstreamed in 2023 (CAIS statement, Bletchley, EO 14110) and shaped OpenAI's and Anthropic's founding.

technologies: CUDA/cuDNN on NVIDIA GPUs (Kepler, Maxwell, Pascal P100)
Deep reinforcement learning with Monte Carlo tree search (AlphaGo)
architectures: Convolutional neural networks (AlexNet, VGG, GoogLeNet, ResNet)

bottlenecks.note: Supervised learning required costly human labels; ImageNet-scale labeling was the template.
A few dozen experts; firms acquired whole labs (DNNresearch 2013, DeepMind 2014).
AlexNet was split across two GPUs; distributed training was immature.
NLP systems remained task-specific; no general text model existed.

perceivedAdvantage: Proprietary user data from consumer platforms (data network effects)
Owning the dominant open-source framework (TensorFlow) to steer developers to one's cloud
Game-playing RL as a demonstration of general intelligence
actualAdvantage: Interpretation (hindsight 2026): NVIDIA's GPU-plus-CUDA position; its FY2017 filing already attributed 145% datacenter growth to deep learning training (ev-ctx-8), and datacenter revenue grew from about $0.83B (FY2017) to $47.5B (FY2024).

Interpretation: in-house research culture and custom silicon at Google (Transformer, TPU) created the technical base for the next decade, though much of the early commercial value from the Transformer was captured by OpenAI and Microsoft.
Interpretation: frameworks commoditized (PyTorch overtook TensorFlow in research), so 'owning the framework' proved not to be a durable moat.
periods.investment: Global corporate AI investment (AI Index, broad definition incl. M&A) was $14.57B in 2013 (ev-ctx-20). NVIDIA's datacenter segment was small: about $0.34B in FY2016 (recalled) rising to $0.83B in FY2017 (ev-ctx-9). Capital went mainly to talent acquisitions (DeepMind, reported ~$400-650M) and to in-house labs at Google, Facebook, Microsoft and Baidu. OpenAI launched with $1B pledged (Dec 2015).

energy.state: Not a constraint; energy appeared only as an application (DeepMind cut Google data-center cooling energy by up to 40%).

semis.state: Gaming GPUs repurposed for deep learning; NVIDIA launched P100/DGX-1 and Google disclosed the TPU.

cloud.state: Training on single servers or small in-house clusters; cloud GPU instances were nascent.

data.state: Labeled datasets (ImageNet) were the key input; web text was used only for embeddings.

architecture.state: CNNs dominated vision; LSTMs with attention dominated sequences; ResNet enabled very deep networks.

training.state: Supervised learning with backprop on GPUs; deep RL with self-play and search for games.

inference.state: Served inside products (photo tagging, speech, translation) at low marginal cost; TPU v1 built for inference.

models.state: Task-specific models; no general-purpose foundation models.

platforms.state: Frameworks (Theano, Caffe, Torch, TensorFlow) became the developer layer.

agents.state: Game-playing RL agents (DQN, AlphaGo) were the showcase of agency.

apps.state: Features in existing products: image search, speech recognition, translation, recommendations.

distribution.state: AI shipped invisibly through incumbent consumer platforms.

economics.state: Talent acqui-hires and in-house labs; little standalone AI revenue.

society.state: Concern limited to existential-risk writers and early fairness/privacy critics; AlphaGo raised national attention in Asia.

underestimated: Speed of progress once compute scaled (AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol years before many forecasts)
Language as the main frontier, versus vision and RL

periods.label: Transformers and pretraining
periods.boundaryRationale: Opens with the Transformer (June 2017), the architecture that ended the CNN/RNN era; ends just before the January 2020 scaling-laws paper converted the scaling bet into a quantitative recipe. Reference range kept; if p2012 is extended to 2017-06, this period would start 2017-06.
periods.consensus: Self-supervised pretraining followed by task fine-tuning (ELMo, GPT-1, BERT) became the NLP default, with BERT-style encoders seen as the practical winner. Leading firms declared 'AI-first' strategies and governments (China 2017) adopted national AI plans. Self-play RL (AlphaGo Zero/AlphaZero) was still widely viewed as the frontier toward general intelligence. Compute for the largest runs was growing extraordinarily fast (3.4-month doubling per OpenAI), and frontier work started to need billions of dollars, prompting OpenAI's capped-profit restructuring and Microsoft's $1B investment.

minorityViews.view: The Bitter Lesson: general methods that leverage computation beat human-knowledge-based approaches; scale the simple thing.
minorityViews.heldBy: Richard Sutton; OpenAI leadership (Sutskever, Amodei, Brockman)
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: the canonical justification for scaling investments 2020-2025.

minorityViews.view: Learning reward functions from human preferences can align powerful models.
minorityViews.heldBy: Paul Christiano, Dario Amodei, Jan Leike, Shane Legg (2017)
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: became RLHF, the post-training step that made InstructGPT and ChatGPT useful.

minorityViews.view: Deep learning is data-hungry, shallow and brittle and cannot reach robust reasoning without symbolic components.
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: reliability, hallucination and reasoning remained real limitations through 2023, but the critique underestimated how far pure scaling plus post-training would go.

minorityViews.view: Training large NLP models has significant energy and carbon costs that should be measured.
minorityViews.heldBy: Emma Strubell, Ananya Ganesh, Andrew McCallum (2019)
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: energy shifted from an ethical footnote to the binding physical constraint on AI buildout by 2024-26.

minorityViews.view: Generative decoder-only language models (GPT) are a better path than bidirectional encoders (BERT).
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: decoder-only generative models became the dominant architecture of every frontier model.

technologies: NVIDIA V100 with Tensor Cores; DGX systems
Pretrained language models (ELMo, GPT-1, BERT, GPT-2)

bottlenecks.item: Compute cost of the largest runs
bottlenecks.note: OpenAI's 2018 analysis showed ~300,000x growth since 2012; non-profit funding was insufficient, prompting OpenAI LP (2019).
Pretraining reduced but did not remove the need for task-specific labels.
GPT-2's staged release made publication policy a governance question.
Huawei's Entity List designation (2019) began the use of chip supply chains as policy levers.

perceivedAdvantage: Proprietary data and 'data network effects' in vertical applications
AI talent concentration in Google, Facebook, Microsoft, Baidu
Autonomous driving and other vertical AI applications
actualAdvantage: Interpretation (hindsight): GPU supply. NVIDIA datacenter revenue rose from $0.83B (FY2017) to $1.93B (FY2018, Volta) and $2.93B (FY2019) (ev-ctx-7, ev-ctx-6), and NVIDIA moved into systems networking via Mellanox.
Interpretation: Microsoft's 2019 $1B OpenAI bet, coupling cloud capacity to a frontier lab, gave it the strongest AI distribution position of 2023.
Interpretation: Google invented the Transformer and BERT but did not capture the generative-model franchise first; publication spread the advantage to others.
periods.investment: NVIDIA datacenter revenue: $1.93B FY2018, $2.93B FY2019 (ev-ctx-7, ev-ctx-6). Microsoft invested $1B in OpenAI (July 2019); NVIDIA agreed to buy Mellanox for $6.9B (March 2019). Year-by-year AI Index private-investment totals for 2017-2019 were not verified in this session; generative-AI private investment was only about $0.84B in 2019 (ev-ctx-21, medium confidence).

energy.state: Still not a constraint; first papers quantified training energy and carbon (Strubell 2019).

semis.state: V100 Tensor Cores made GPUs AI-specific; TPU v2/v3 offered on Google Cloud; US-China chip tensions began.

cloud.state: Large training runs moved to dedicated cloud clusters; Microsoft-OpenAI Azure exclusivity (2019).

data.state: Unlabeled web text became the main pretraining input; GDPR (2018) raised data-protection obligations.

architecture.state: Transformer replaced RNNs in NLP within two years.

training.state: Pretrain-then-fine-tune established; self-play RL at its peak (AlphaZero).

inference.state: BERT-sized models served in search and ads; inference cost not yet a strategic issue.

models.state: Pretrained language models (BERT, GPT-2) became reusable backbones but not products.

platforms.state: PyTorch and TensorFlow competed; model hubs and pretrained checkpoints spread.

periods.label: Scaling laws and foundation models
periods.boundaryRationale: Starts with Kaplan et al.'s scaling laws (23 Jan 2020), which made capability a predictable function of compute, quickly followed by GPT-3 (May 2020). Ends before Chinchilla, InstructGPT and diffusion (March-August 2022) changed the recipe and the public face of AI. Proposed revision: the technical turn arguably comes at 2022-03 (Chinchilla/InstructGPT), so a 2020-01 to 2022-02 range would be equally defensible.
periods.consensus: Larger language models predictably get better (scaling laws), and GPT-3 showed a single model could perform many tasks via prompting (few-shot in-context learning). Stanford's 'foundation models' framing (Aug 2021) captured the view that a few broad models would be adapted to many uses. Commercial uses were limited to APIs, copywriting startups and the Copilot preview; most enterprises viewed LLMs as experimental. The pandemic accelerated digitization and a broad chip shortage made supply chains a political issue.

periods.label: Generative AI goes mainstream
periods.boundaryRationale: Reference start 2022-01 is supported: the technical and infrastructure pivots (chain-of-thought Jan 2022, Chinchilla and InstructGPT Mar 2022, H100 Mar 2022, diffusion image models Apr-Aug 2022, US chip export controls Oct 2022) all precede ChatGPT. ChatGPT (30 Nov 2022) is the true boundary for public adoption, capital and policy: Microsoft's $10B (Jan 2023), generative-AI private investment rising ~8-9x to $25.2B in 2023, NVIDIA's datacenter jump (FY2024 +217%) and the 2023 governance wave all follow it. Proposed revision: keep p2022 at 2022-01 to 2023-12 but mark 2022-11-30 as an intra-period boundary (sub-phases 'generative capability' 2022-01..2022-11 and 'mass adoption' 2022-12..2023-12); for capital-flow charts, use 2022-11 as the break. The end at 2023-12 is well supported by Gemini (Dec 6), the EU AI Act deal (Dec 8), Mixtral (Dec 11) and the NYT lawsuit (Dec 27).
periods.consensus: Generative AI became a mass-market product category: ChatGPT reached an estimated 100M monthly users within two months and GPT-4 set a new capability bar. Chinchilla shifted scaling toward more data per parameter, and RLHF post-training was recognized as essential for usable assistants. The industry believed a small number of well-capitalized frontier labs paired with hyperscalers would dominate, with GPU supply (H100) the key constraint. By late 2023 governments moved from voluntary commitments to binding measures (US EO 14110, EU AI Act deal) and extinction-risk concerns were voiced by lab leaders themselves.
